newsitem.title: USA: Tower sees analysts cutting estimates.
newsitem.headline: Tower sees analysts cutting estimates.

text.p: Tower Automotive Inc said Tuesday it expects the consensus of analysts' estimates for its 1997 earnings to be cut to $2.15-$2.20 a share from the current $2.24 due a Chrysler Corp strike.
Tower, a maker of automotive chassis, frames and suspensions, said it expects 1997 results to be hurt by the recent strike at a Chrysler engine plant.

"I think those numbers will be adjusted down slightly as analysts incorporate the impact of the second quarter strike at Chrysler," Tower corporate development vice president Scott Rued said following a presentation at the Piper Jaffray Investors conference here.
A range of "$2.15-$2.20 will be the consensus estimate," he said.
Indianapolis-based Tower reported earnings of $1.55 a share for 1996.
Rued said the company's recent acquisition of Automotive Products Co would reduce Tower's operating margins in the near term.

"Tower's historic operating margins are 10 percent, but APC's margins are a little less than that," Rued said. "So our operating margins will be below 10 percent in the second quarter. Our goal is to bring that back up to an overall rate of 10 pecent. We expect to get there in 18 months."
Automotive frame maker APC was acquired by Tower for $625 million in a deal that closed April 18.
Tower acquired SIMES, a Turan, Italy-based automotive components manufacturer, for $70 million in a deal that closed on May 9.
Those two acquisitions raised the company's long-term debt-to-capital ratio.

"We funded the acquisitions of both companies through the combination of a stock offering and debt," Rued said. "Our long-term debt-to-total-capital at the end of this (second) quarter will be aobut 45 percent."
